metadata.name: Shadow AI agent discovery estate benchmark corpus
metadata.estate: Vantor Logistics (fictional): vantor.example, devices dev-laptop-01/dev-laptop-02/win-laptop-03/build-runner-3, AWS 210987654321, GCP vantor-ml, Azure sub-vantor-1, k8s vantor-prod
metadata.labeling: Every entity was authored together with its artifacts and labeled from the artifact's vendor semantics before any tool ran on the merged corpus. Artifact formats were verified parse-clean against ShadowScan's offline loaders during authoring (completeness only); labels were never changed because a tool missed or flagged an entity, and the corpus deliberately keeps positives known to exceed documented detection and negatives known to be over-flagged, including by ShadowScan itself. This is author-written labeling with evidence pointers, not independent human review.

classes.positive: a genuine AI agent or AI usage per the artifact's vendor semantics
classes.control: clearly non-AI; any attributed in-scope finding is a false positive
classes.nearmiss: AI-adjacent vocabulary or shape without AI technology; flagging it is a false positive

metadata.attribution: Predictions attach to entities by anchor substring (longest anchor wins), or, for unit-bound runs, by exact or generic fact match within the unit. Unattributed in-scope predictions are charged as false positives.
metadata.authoring_additions: After the nine surface authors finished, agent session transcripts were added to the dev-laptop-01 and dev-laptop-02 home trees (.claude/projects, .claude/history, .cursor/projects agent-transcripts, .codex/sessions, .codex/history) so installed agents carry the at-rest artifacts a real endpoint would have; estate/registry/ and estate/services/ were added; no labels changed.
metadata.errata: v1 label-completeness audit (every runnable tool's first pass, before the published run): a bare 'VS Code is present' client row, emitted by endpoint inventory tools for the ~/.vscode extensions directory, is tolerated estate-wide — the corpus models the AI extension inside VS Code as the entity, not the editor itself. No entity labels were changed.

entities.rationale: pyproject declares crewai, crewai-tools and langchain-openai, and crew.py builds a two-agent CrewAI crew on ChatOpenAI with OPENAI_API_KEY: a multi-agent AI system by PyPI package and import semantics.

LangGraph StateGraph calling the Anthropic SDK, with a committed .mcp.json (Claude Code client configuration by path convention) and a CLAUDE.md instruction file. mcp:sdk is tolerated because the .mcp.json names @modelcontextprotocol server packages in npx args.

package.json declares the Vercel AI SDK ('ai' plus @ai-sdk/openai) and @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, the source builds a tool-calling assistant and an MCP server, and public/.well-known/agent.json is an A2A agent card by path convention.

Terraform provisions an aws_bedrockagent_agent on an Anthropic Claude foundation model plus a Titan-embedding knowledge base, and an Azure OpenAI cognitive account with a gpt-35-turbo deployment whose endpoint is *.openai.azure.com: managed AI resources by IaC semantics. provider:openai is tolerated for the gpt-35-turbo deployment's OpenAI-family model name.

Committed n8n workflow exports with @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain agent nodes chatting through OpenAI and Anthropic models: AI-powered low-code flows by n8n node semantics. framework:langchain is tolerated because the node type string embeds 'langchain' without a LangChain dependency.

Go module requiring langchaingo and go-openai, an etabot talking to a local Ollama at localhost:11434, and a committed .cursor/mcp.json (Cursor MCP client configuration by path). Hard: Go import resolution and host-based Ollama evidence exceed many tools' documented code-scanning coverage.
Ordinary Flask + SQLAlchemy warehouse management service: no AI dependency, import, endpoint, model identifier or agent configuration anywhere in the tree.
Static documentation site built with lodash and marked: plain JavaScript content tooling with no AI packages, hosts or configuration.

Embedded firmware for the Microchip MCP2515 CAN controller: 'MCP' vocabulary saturates identifiers, comments and docs but refers to the chip, not Model Context Protocol. Any mcp:* finding here is a false positive; keyword-driven tools are known to over-flag this shape.

Zero-dependency user-agent parser whose README documents AI crawler tokens (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai) and whose test fixtures contain those UA strings; the code has no AI package, import or provider hostname. Documentation-only mentions never count; fixture-driven provider facts are tolerated, anything else flagged here is a false positive.
Fireflies.ai meeting notetaker OIDC app with live user tokens: an AI SaaS OAuth grant by vendor semantics.
Custom M2M service app (client_credentials + token-exchange, private_key_jwt, okta.users.read grant) whose label names an AI negotiation agent.
Glean AI enterprise search SSO'd via SAML; an AI product integration even without OAuth scopes.
Gemini the cryptocurrency exchange (redirect to exchange.gemini.com), not Google Gemini; name-matching tools are known to over-flag it.
Tenant-owned service principal for an AutoGen email agent holding the app-only Mail.ReadWrite Graph role.
Managed identity that an incident-triage agent runs as; a machine identity serving an AI agent.
OpenAI's ChatGPT service principal with a user-consented oauth2PermissionGrant for Files/Sites read: AI SaaS consent by vendor semantics.
Ordinary third-party Workday SSO service principal with no grants or roles; clearly non-AI.
'aix' is the IBM AIX product code of a billing export pipeline, not an AI workload; flagging it on the 'ai' substring is a false positive.
Otter.ai notetaker OAuth client granted calendar and gmail readonly by two users: AI meeting assistant with data access.
Reclaim.ai is an AI scheduling assistant holding calendar access; it sits outside common product signature lists, so detecting it as AI may exceed documented capabilities.
Expense tool holding only userinfo.email; ordinary non-AI OAuth client.
Non-interactive M2M client described as a CrewAI rate-negotiation agent with a client grant on the core API.
Plain SPA with authorization_code flow and no AI traits; ordinary web app.
MCP2515 is a CAN-bus controller chip; this telemetry bridge M2M client has no AI technology, yet 'mcp' substring matchers and machine-client heuristics are known to over-flag it.
Entra app-only token (idtyp=app) with Files.ReadWrite.All and an agent_id claim: a service token minted for an agent.
Okta service token (cid==sub) carrying an act claim for priya plus an agent_id: an agent acting on a user's behalf.
Kubernetes service-account token of the yard-router agent in the agent-runtime namespace; tying a workload token to an AI agent via namespace semantics may exceed documented detection.
Plain short-lived human Google OIDC token with no scopes or agent claims; classifies as human at ~0.05 confidence.
LiteLLM proxy caller whose requests carry function-tool definitions and tool_calls finish reasons under a LangChain user agent: an agentic caller per LiteLLM spend-log semantics.
LiteLLM caller doing plain chat completions with end-user attribution (nika@vantor.example) and no tool use: real LLM usage, not an agent.
Bedrock model-invocation-log caller from an assumed-role ARN issuing Converse requests with a toolConfig and tool_use stop reasons: an agent loop per Bedrock invocation-log semantics.
Azure OpenAI diagnostics caller (appid claim) whose requests carry a Microsoft Agent Framework user agent against a chat deployment: an agent-framework workload per Azure diagnostic-log semantics.
Egress-proxy caller with a CrewAI framework user agent POSTing chat completions to api.openai.com: an agent-framework caller observed at the network edge.
OpenTelemetry GenAI spans naming gen_ai.agent.name and an invoke_agent operation for this service: an instrumented agent per OTel GenAI semantic conventions.

Caller POSTing to /generate on an internal self-hosted HuggingFace Text Generation Inference host (tgi-yard): genuine LLM inference, but the unlisted host and non-standard path sit outside known-host and inference-path lists, so it may exceed documented detection capabilities.
Intranet wiki page fetches (GET /index.html and wiki pages on wiki.vantor.example): ordinary non-AI traffic with no model, LLM host or inference path.

Chrome browser users of the intranet helpdesk live-chat widget (human-to-human chat, no model anywhere); its /api/chat path matches Ollama-style inference-path heuristics, a shape discovery tools are known to over-flag.
Ordinary HTTP spans for a nightly billing cron service with no GenAI attributes at all: plainly non-AI telemetry.

An audit dashboard GETting /v1/threads/.../runs on api.openai.com: a read-only listing of hosted run metadata, not an invocation and not inference, yet the path and host make tools report an AI caller.

Market-data polling of api.gemini.com, the Gemini cryptocurrency exchange REST API (GET /v1/pubticker/btcusd): the Gemini name is AI-adjacent vocabulary with no AI technology, so flagging it is a false positive.

Copilot Studio bot with generative answers (GptComponentMetadata component) published with no authentication; the one sanctioned/registered low-code agent, inventoried as power-platform:bot:bot-hrhelper-v7q2k.
Power Automate flow referencing the shared_azureopenai connector on a recurrence schedule: AI usage per Power Platform connector semantics.
Scheduled file-copy flow using only office365 and sharepointonline connectors: ordinary automation, no AI connector or signature.
Salesforce BotDefinition with an active BotVersion describing an Agentforce service agent: an AI agent by Salesforce object semantics.
GenAiPlannerDefinition (Agentforce planner, Tooling API object): an AI agent definition by Salesforce semantics, collected less often than BotDefinition.

sys_hub_flow that merely deprovisions unused Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses with user-table steps; it invokes no Now Assist or generative action, but the AI product name in its title is known to over-flag name-matching tools.
n8n workflow built on the langchain AI Agent node with an OpenAI chat model and an HTTP tool, running on a schedule: an AI agent by n8n node semantics.

n8n workflow with no AI node type: its only LLM use is a plain httpRequest node POSTing chat completions to a self-hosted vLLM endpoint with a qwen2.5 model. Genuine AI usage per the request body, but it may exceed node-type and vendor-domain detection.
Cron-triggered Google Sheets/Drive backup workflow: ordinary automation with no AI nodes or parameters.

Gmail-to-Drive attachment filing zap: ordinary non-AI automation.

Zap title contains the standalone word AI (it forwards a newsletter about AI) but its only steps are Gmail and Email by Zapier; keyword tools matching the title over-flag it, which is a false positive by Zapier step semantics.

evidence: lowcode/workato_recipes.json#rcp-claimsgenai-w6r9t provider workato_genai in config and code block

entities.rationale: Workato recipe whose config and code use the workato_genai provider to draft claim responses: AI usage by Workato connector semantics.

Scheduled recipe pulling trades from api.gemini.com, the Gemini cryptocurrency exchange, over plain http and posting journals to NetSuite; no AI technology, but the Gemini name and domain are classic over-flag bait for AI-name matching.
Anthropic Claude Slack app approved in the vantor workspace with a bot user and chat:write/channels:history scopes; an installed AI assistant per Slack app semantics.
Pending app_request for Read.ai, an AI meeting-notes product; a requested-but-not-yet-installed AI app is still discoverable AI usage pressure in the workspace.

Wudpecker is a real AI meeting notetaker (wudpecker.io), so the approved app is genuinely AI per vendor semantics, but it holds only commands/incoming-webhook scopes, has no bot user, and its name sits outside common signature packs - a positive that may exceed documented detection capability.
Internal Freight Status Webhook app with only commands and incoming-webhook scopes and no bot user; an ordinary non-AI workflow integration (verified non-finding scope set).
Org-wide (distributionMethod organization) declarative Copilot agent with a bot and RSC permissions; a tenant-published AI agent per Teams app-catalog semantics.
Otter.ai store app installed in the Sales team with a bot; a third-party AI meeting transcription bot per vendor semantics.
Store app named Mistral Route Planner after the Mediterranean wind: a deterministic lane-planning tool with no bot and no AI technology; flagging it on the 'mistral' token is a false positive.
CodeRabbit-style AI code-review GitHub App installed org-wide with pull_requests:write; a sanctioned (registered) AI reviewer, resource github:installation:70110427.
Claude coding-agent GitHub App installation with contents/actions write; an AI coding agent with code-execution capability per GitHub App semantics.
Renovate dependency-update bot: write-capable automation but not AI technology; a classic non-AI bot that naive scanners over-flag.
BI exporter app whose slug 'dataai-export' contains the substring 'ai' without any AI technology; flagging it on the token is a false positive.
Glean enterprise AI search/assistant app user-installed on Confluence; an AI app per Atlassian UPM semantics.
Ordinary third-party Timesheets reporting plugin for Jira with no AI functionality.
Workspace-owned Notion bot integration named Claude; an AI assistant connected to the workspace per Notion user-object semantics.
Custom non-AI integration bot that mirrors Jira tickets into Notion; tools that report every Notion bot will over-flag it, but it is not AI per vendor semantics - a deliberate hard negative.
Fathom AI Notetaker installed account-wide with meeting:read and recording:read; an AI meeting assistant per Zoom marketplace semantics.
Internal Whiteboard Sync utility holding only user:read, deliberately adjacent to the meeting:read policy boundary; not AI and verified as a non-finding scope set.
Perplexity marketplace app with drive.readonly data-access scope installed by tom; an AI answer-engine OAuth app per marketplace export semantics.
Gemini Trust Company cryptocurrency exchange portal (gemini.com) with only a userinfo scope; the Gemini name is AI-adjacent vocabulary, not AI technology, so flagging it is a false positive.

A PREPARED Amazon Bedrock agent on Claude 3.5 Sonnet with two enabled action groups, a knowledge base and a prod alias: a managed AI agent by AWS semantics. Registered in the estate inventory; its ShadowScan resource is the agentArn.
A READY Bedrock AgentCore runtime serving a containerized claims-intake agent over public HTTP with an Anthropic API key in its environment: an AI agent runtime by AWS AgentCore semantics.
A READY Bedrock AgentCore gateway speaking MCP with two tool targets (OpenAPI and Lambda): agentic tool infrastructure by AWS AgentCore semantics.
A Lambda function carrying ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and a langchain-deps layer: a custom LLM workload with no managed-AI resource type, so cloud-ai:generic.
A Vertex AI Agent Engine (reasoning engine) built on google-adk with query/stream_query methods: a managed AI agent by GCP semantics.
A Dialogflow CX agent with generative settings (gemini-1.5-flash) and a start playbook: a generative conversational agent by Dialogflow semantics.
A Microsoft.CognitiveServices account of kind OpenAI with a live gpt-4o deployment, public network access and key auth enabled: Azure OpenAI usage by Azure resource semantics.

An Azure AI Foundry agent (gpt-4o, file_search + code_interpreter tools) in the freight-ops project: an AI agent by Foundry data-plane semantics, which needs agent-level (not just ARM) enumeration to find.

A Deployment in cluster vantor-prod running the ollama/ollama image with a GPU request and port 11434: a self-hosted LLM runtime by image semantics. The runner config supplies cluster: vantor-prod, so findings land at k8s:vantor-prod/ml-serving/Deployment/linehaul-ollama-g5v.

A genuine vLLM OpenAI-compatible server (private-registry vllm-serving image, --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, port 8000) whose GPU sits only under limits and whose env names carry no provider markers: a real k8s AI workload that sits outside documented image/env/GPU-request detection heuristics.
A plain Node.js Lambda that renders warehouse label PDFs; no AI env, layers, images or naming. Flagging it is a false positive.
An ordinary StorageV2 account for freight documents; a non-AI Azure resource type that inventory scans should pass over.
A stock nginx Deployment serving the fleet web portal; no AI image, env or GPU. Clearly non-AI infrastructure.

A finance Lambda whose name starts with 'ai-' but that only rolls up Cost Explorer allocation tags: AI vocabulary with no AI technology (no AI env, layers or runtime). Name-keyed discovery over-flags it.

A plain python:3.12-slim Deployment that exports SageMaker billing data to a finops bucket: the name carries AI-product vocabulary but the workload runs no AI technology. A known over-flag trap for name-based k8s scanners.

A Cloud Run service syncing settlements with the Gemini cryptocurrency exchange (api.gemini.com, GEMINI_EXCHANGE_API_KEY): 'Gemini' here is the crypto exchange, not Google's model, so flagging it as AI is a false positive. Env-name and name heuristics are known to over-flag it.

Claude Code user-scope state (~/.claude.json with MCP servers), settings with a permissive approval posture, and a non-empty subagents directory: a genuinely configured coding agent. Registered in the estate agent registry, so it should reconcile as non-shadow.
Cursor's documented user-scope MCP configuration file with two configured servers; vendor semantics make this an installed AI coding client.
Windsurf's documented user-scope MCP configuration with the same two servers as Cursor, giving deliberate cross-tool overlap on one device.
Claude Desktop's Linux user-scope configuration file with one MCP server configured: an installed AI desktop client.
A populated Ollama manifest store (two model tags, one library and one custom namespace) is a local model store per Ollama's on-disk layout.
OpenAI Codex CLI's user-scope TOML configuration with an [mcp_servers.*] table: an installed AI coding client.
Gemini CLI's documented user-scope settings file with an MCP server configured: an installed AI coding client.
Continue's user-scope YAML configuration with a model block and an MCP server list; several endpoint scanners are documented to miss Continue.
An installed GitHub Copilot VS Code extension directory following the publisher.name-version marketplace layout: an AI editor extension.
A Chrome extension whose manifest name is the AI assistant product Claude, installed in the Default profile: an AI browser extension.
Claude Desktop's Windows (AppData/Roaming) configuration with one MCP server; the Windows layout inside a snapshotted home tree trips scanners that only probe Linux paths.
Amazon Q Developer's documented user-scope MCP configuration under ~/.aws/amazonq: an installed AI coding client.
Cline's MCP settings under the VS Code globalStorage path on a Windows-layout home; Cline is documented as missed by several endpoint scanners, and the deep AppData path makes it harder still.
A .gguf model file inside LM Studio's documented models directory is a populated local model store per LM Studio's layout.

One MCP server identity (the pinned npx GitHub server) configured across ten client configuration files on all three devices; per MCP semantics this is one configured server, counted once estate-wide.

A custom stdio MCP server built in-house, configured in three clients on dev-laptop-01 and present (authenticated, with benign tools) in the offline MCP tool inventory export: one server identity estate-wide.

An unauthenticated remote MCP server whose tool description embeds a prompt-injection (tool-poisoning) phrase; recognizing the poisoned description exceeds many tools' documented detection capabilities.
An Ollama runtime export from build-runner-3 bound to 0.0.0.0:11434 (exposed beyond localhost) serving two models, one of them a custom fine-tune: a local LLM model store per Ollama's API semantics.
An eBPF network event showing a python3 process in pod freight-worker-6k9td connecting to api.openai.com:443: a running process using an AI provider per the telemetry's own semantics.
uBlock Origin is an ordinary content blocker with no AI capability; flagging a mainstream non-AI browser extension is a false positive.
A backup-sync process talking to internal object storage on port 8443 is ordinary infrastructure traffic with no AI host or local-LLM port; flagging it is a false positive.
A standard htop configuration directory is an ordinary non-AI dotfile location that no endpoint discovery tool should flag.

A crypto-exchange wallet extension named Gemini Wallet shares a word with Google's AI product but has no AI technology; name-matching tools are known to over-flag it, and flagging it is a false positive.
A ~/.cursorstats directory belongs to a terminal-cursor statistics plugin, not the Cursor editor; a tool that globs for .cursor* paths over-flags it.

A stale .bak backup of a removed client configuration is not a live config at any documented location; no client reads it, so flagging it as an installed AI client or configured MCP server is a false positive.
Full DNS+TLS+flow chain from one client to api.anthropic.com with five connections 6 seconds apart (agent-loop cadence): unambiguous AI API traffic by Zeek log semantics.
A single DNS lookup of api.openai.com with no TLS or flow corroboration: still a genuine AI service contact by DNS semantics, but weaker evidence than a full chain.
DNS, TLS SNI and flow to api2.cursor.sh, the Cursor coding-agent backend: an agent-service contact, not a consumer chat app, by the vendor's endpoint semantics.

Plain TCP flows from one client to an internal host on 11434 (Ollama's default API port) with no DNS or TLS evidence at all: a real self-hosted LLM contact that only port-heuristic attribution can reach, likely beyond documented detection capabilities of name-based tools.
A resolver-export DNS lookup of generativelanguage.googleapis.com, the Gemini API (AI Studio) endpoint outside Cloud IAM: genuine Gemini API usage by Google's endpoint semantics.
A DNS lookup of openrouter.ai, a multi-provider LLM aggregator API: genuine AI service usage by the vendor's sole purpose.
A client browsing www.vantor.example and github.com over full DNS+TLS+flow chains: ordinary corporate and developer traffic with no AI service involved; flagging it is a false positive.
A DNS lookup of slack.com, an ordinary collaboration platform: non-AI traffic that should be counted and never stored or reported.

DNS and TLS SNI to api.gemini.com, the Gemini cryptocurrency exchange API, which shares its name with Google's Gemini model family: a hard negative that keyword-matching discovery tools are known to over-flag; attributing it to an AI service is a false positive.

A DNS lookup of claude-monet-exhibit.org, an art exhibition site whose name contains the substring 'claude': AI-adjacent vocabulary with no AI technology; substring matching against model names would wrongly flag it.

A node process running @anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js is the Claude Code coding agent actually executing as dana on dev-laptop-01; it lifecycle-links with the endpoint author's Claude Code config for the same home.

npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github is a running MCP server (the launcher must be unwrapped to the package name); it lifecycle-links with the Cursor MCP config declaring the same package on this device.
/usr/local/bin/ollama serve is the Ollama local model server running as marcus on dev-laptop-02: a live local LLM runtime per Ollama's own semantics (serve starts the API server).

A CrowdStrike Falcon flat telemetry row (ComputerName/UserName/ImageFileName/CommandLine) for the aider coding agent running against a local Ollama model; tools that only parse osquery event lines will miss this vendor format, but it is a genuinely running AI pair-programming agent.

python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server is the vLLM OpenAI-compatible model server running as the ci user on build-runner-3; detection requires resolving the -m module through the python launcher, not the executable name.

A Microsoft Defender DeviceProcessEvents-shaped row: ollama.exe serve running as priya on win-laptop-03. The executable lives in FolderPath with FileName separate and the command line is quoted Windows-style, so it may exceed detection by tools that only understand osquery rows; by Ollama semantics the model server is running.
An ordinary nginx web server master process on build-runner-3: no AI technology of any kind; flagging routine infrastructure daemons is a false positive.

A one-shot 'ollama list' CLI invocation: by Ollama semantics this only queries installed models and runs no model server, so nothing AI is running. A deliberate hard negative: discovery tools that match on the ollama binary name alone are known to over-flag it.
/usr/bin/claudette-backup is a backup daemon whose name merely contains 'claude' as a substring; it has no AI technology, so a substring match on the binary name is a false positive.
python3 train_model.py is a classical ML training script with ML-ish vocabulary (model, epochs) but no agent, LLM runtime or MCP component; flagging it as an AI agent process is a false positive.
